challenges.name: debug-crashloop-quiz
challenges.title: Read a pod that keeps restarting
challenges.description: Three statements about how the on-call engineer read Rice Rocket's crash-looping api pods. Decide whether each one is true.
hints: After a restart there are two containers in the story: the one running now and the one that died. Which one does `kubectl logs` read by default, and which flag reads the other?
Compare `state.waiting.reason` with `lastState.terminated.reason`. One tells you what the kubelet is doing now, the other what happened to the last run.
Some failures happen before the process starts at all. Would restarting the container change the Secret it reads?

questions.question:
The api pod has restarted four times. The engineer runs:

```text
$ kubectl get pod api-7b9c6d5f4-k2x8p -n rice-rocket
NAME                  READY   STATUS             RESTARTS      AGE
api-7b9c6d5f4-k2x8p   0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   4 (31s ago)   3m12s
$ kubectl logs api-7b9c6d5f4-k2x8p -n rice-rocket
{"level":30,"msg":"loading config"}
```

Statement: "`kubectl logs` without flags shows the output of the container that crashed, so the crash happened right after `loading config` and printed nothing."
questions.explanation: False. `kubectl logs` reads the **current** container: the one the kubelet started after the last crash, which has only just begun (or is waiting in back-off). The run that died is read with `kubectl logs api-7b9c6d5f4-k2x8p --previous`. Its last lines usually hold the error. The misconception is that a pod has one log across restarts.

questions.question:
`kubectl describe pod` for the same pod shows:

```text
    State:          Waiting
      Reason:       CrashLoopBackOff
    Last State:     Terminated
      Reason:       Error
      Exit Code:    1
    Restart Count:  4
Events:
  Normal   Pulled   2m   kubelet  Container image "ghcr.io/rice-rocket/api:1.5.0" already present on machine
  Warning  BackOff  31s  kubelet  Back-off restarting failed container api in pod api-7b9c6d5f4-k2x8p
```

Statement: "CrashLoopBackOff is not the cause. It means the kubelet is waiting longer and longer (up to 5 minutes) between restarts; the cause is in Last State (exit code 1: the app exited with an error) and in the previous container's log."
questions.explanation: True. `CrashLoopBackOff` is a waiting reason: the container keeps exiting, so the kubelet restarts it with an exponential back-off (10s, 20s, 40s, ... capped at 5 minutes). It says nothing about why. `Last State: Terminated` holds the exit code and reason of the run that died: 1 is an error from the app itself, 137 with `OOMKilled` is the memory limit, 137 or 143 after `failed liveness probe` events is the kubelet killing it. The misconception is to search the internet for "CrashLoopBackOff" as if it were an error message.

questions.question:
After a Secret was recreated by hand, a new rollout is stuck:

```text
$ kubectl get pods -n rice-rocket -l app=api
NAME                  READY   STATUS                       RESTARTS   AGE
api-6d8f7c9b5-zt4qw   0/1     CreateContainerConfigError   0          2m
$ kubectl describe pod api-6d8f7c9b5-zt4qw -n rice-rocket | tail -2
  Warning  Failed  12s (x9 over 2m)  kubelet  Error: couldn't find key db_password in Secret rice-rocket/api-secrets
$ kubectl get secret api-secrets -n rice-rocket -o jsonpath='{.data}' | jq 'keys'
["db-password", "jwt-secret"]
```

Statement: "The container never started: the Deployment asks for the key `db_password` but the recreated Secret has `db-password`. Deleting the pod or restarting the rollout will not help until the key name matches."
questions.explanation: True. `CreateContainerConfigError` happens before the process starts, while the kubelet builds the container's environment from `secretKeyRef`. There is no log and the restart count stays 0. A new pod reads the same Secret and fails the same way. Fix either the Secret (recreate it with the key `db_password`) or the Deployment's `key:`; the waiting pod then starts on the next retry. The misconception is that every not-ready pod is fixed by a restart.

challenges.name: pod-triage-script
challenges.title: Fix the pod triage script
challenges.description: Rice Rocket's on-call bot runs `runbooks/triage.js` on every pod that is not ready and posts its answer in the incident channel. Last week it gave wrong advice four times: it quoted the log of the fresh container instead of the one that died, called an OOMKilled api an app crash, missed ImagePullBackOff and CreateContainerConfigError entirely, and never noticed that the kubelet was killing the api for failed liveness probes. The editor holds the fixed script with its key blocks missing, each marked by a `// [ ]` line; some pieces are last week's buggy versions. `triage(pod, events, logs)` gets `kubectl get pod -o json`, the pod's events (oldest first) and `{ current, previous }` logs, and must return `{ cause, evidence, next }` for the first container whose `ready` is false (`Healthy`, "all containers ready", "nothing to do" when there is none), checking in this order: `state.waiting.reason` `ImagePullBackOff` or `ErrImagePull` (cause `ImagePullBackOff`) and `CreateContainerConfigError`, both with the waiting message as evidence; `lastState.terminated.reason` `OOMKilled` (evidence `exit code <code> (OOMKilled) after <restartCount> restarts`); a `Killing` event whose message says `failed liveness probe` (cause `LivenessProbe`, evidence the last event message starting with `Liveness probe failed`); otherwise, if the container has a last state or restarts, `AppError` with the last non-empty line of the previous log (or `exit code <code>`); otherwise `Starting` with the waiting reason. `next` comes from the `NEXT` table. Run grades it on recorded pods.
hints: For each recorded pod, write down which field holds the answer: `state.waiting`, `lastState.terminated` or the events. Which of them did last week's script never read?

The order matters: a container that was never created has no last state; an OOM kill and a liveness kill both end with a non-zero exit code, but only one of them has a `reason` that says so; the events tell the other one apart.

A triage for a node instead of a pod: `const pressure = node.status.conditions.find((c) => c.type === "MemoryPressure" && c.status === "True"); if (pressure) return { cause: "MemoryPressure", evidence: pressure.message };` and for the kubelet log it reads the last line of the **previous** boot (`journalctl -b -1`), not the current one.
